heading: 4.7 Exploratory Objective Seven: evaluation of AIR
objective: To explore the diagnostic performance and supported clinical and recorded-cost context of AIR alone and in comparison with MAS and the two MAS–hs-CRP combinations.
methods: Histopathology was the reference standard: acute, suppurative, phlegmonous, gangrenous and perforated appendicitis were positive; reactive lymphoid hyperplasia was negative. Simple appendicitis comprised the first three positive categories and complicated appendicitis comprised gangrenous or perforated disease. Recorded AIR ≥9 was positive; low 0–4, intermediate 5–8 and high 9–12 categories were retained. The observed scores were integer values from 4 to 10 without missing values. Original score construction and the full protocol were unavailable, so the stored AIR score was not reconstructed. MAS ≥7 and hs-CRP >3 mg/L were positive. “MAS and hs-CRP” required both tests to be positive; “MAS or hs-CRP” required either test to be positive. Neither combination was designated the single prespecified primary rule. All four strategies used 85 complete records. Wilson/log intervals describe proportions/likelihood ratios. Exact paired McNemar tests use Holm adjustment across nine contrasts; one paired DeLong AUC comparison is separate. AUC intervals use 1,000 stratified bootstrap resamples. Age contrasts use independent Fisher exact tests with Holm correction across three measures.
finalParagraph: The recorded AIR score showed discrimination across thresholds, but AIR ≥9 had low sensitivity in this cohort. Age and severity analyses were imprecise, and neither strategy-specific cost effects nor AIR-related confidence changes could be estimated. The findings are exploratory and do not replace the six primary objectives.
